summary: A dense worker-placement/bidding game where the modular board means the available action spots shift each round, forcing constant replanning around a tight economic engine of materials, patrons, art, and building levels. It rewards efficient multi-turn planning and punishes players who get outbid or locked out of key spots, with a real risk of losing workers on the 'free' actions.
praised: Clever modular board that changes the game every session
Tight, interlocking economic engine with meaningful decisions
High replayability due to variable action availability
Satisfying tension between free-but-risky and paid-but-safe actions
criticised: Steep rules overhead and learning curve for new players
Can feel fiddly/overloaded with tracks and sub-systems
Downtime and analysis paralysis in higher player counts
Bidding/blocking can feel harsh for newer players caught unaware

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via worker placement and bidding

scoring.why: Points come from multiple interacting systems — building levels, art sales, patrons, and prestige from the action board — so the winner is usually whoever balances several engines rather than maxing one.
